title: Wade, Johnny Dodds, Georgie Boy and Jimmy Noone
summary: They discuss Wade's playing, Dodds and Bechet-style players, and Jimmy Newton known as Jimbo.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, I say he was, you know how he played?

I heard him, yeah, 1945. How did he play? Pretty good. Yeah, he was a good player. He hadn't been playing, he'd been working in a shipyard or something out in California during the war, and he went back to the clarinet, he sounded a little bit like Johnny Dodds. Do you remember Johnny Dodds?

Yeah, I know Johnny, he was a routine. I didn't count him. Now when I get to that class, on that kind of class was Sidney Bechet at that time, they all would play like Sidney Bechet, Johnny Dodds, Muley, Muley Bond. Well, they all could jam at that time around the same thing. It was old time, but they played in, uh, Georgie Boy. Yeah, I never knew him.

Georgie Boy played clarinet too, he was with that bunch. What did you do? Well, uh, my other boy I never did mention too, he was in the band with my daddy. Had a good clarinet band, was Picoosecar Lunderville. What?
Oh, no, no. He was the brother-in-law of Sidney Veen, clarinet, Lunderville. Oh, he was a good musician. Did you ever know Jimmy Newton? I think they called him Jimbo. Yeah, Jimbo.
Jimbo. Yeah, I know what I mean. Did he play much around here?

Oh, yeah, he used to play at Southern State, played a whole lot of clarinet, he was alright. I don't know, I couldn't bet on his music ability, I mean on the music, but I could tell you when coming out of the playing, it took a good man to move him. I knew he was just called.
He had that barrension, you see. Oh, he had a whole lot of fast fingering. Fast fingering. Fast fingering. I don't know how he was here. He was better here, because he was playing with boys.
He had one of the best read sections in Chicago, great Jimmy Noon. Yeah, I knew him up there.
Do you know anything about where he came from?
Because I never got to talk to him very much, maybe two minutes or so.
